Let $m=\min_i f(i)$. Since $|f(i)-f(i+1)|\le1$, the sequence $f(1),\dots,f(100)$ takes every integer between its minimum $m$ and its maximum. Because $f(f(i))=100$, $100$ belongs to the image, so $[m,100]\subseteq\operatorname{Im}f$. The condition $f(f(i))=100$ also means every value in the image is sent to $100$; hence $f(x)=100$ for all $x\in[m,100]$. To minimize the sum we take no extra points mapping to $100$, i.e. $f(i)=100$ exactly for $i\in[m,100]$.

For $i<m$ we must have $f(i)\in[m,100]$ with $|f(i)-f(i+1)|\le1$ and $f(m)=100$. The pointwise smallest feasible choice is
$$f(i)=\max\{m,\;100-(m-i)\},\qquad i=1,\dots,m-1,$$
which decreases by $1$ from $100$ down to $m$ and then stays at $m$.

This gives
$$S(m)=\begin{cases}
100^2-\dfrac{m(m-1)}2, & m\le50,\\[6pt]
\dfrac{3m^2-401m+30100}2, & m\ge51.
\end{cases}$$
For $m\le50$, $S(m)$ decreases, so the smallest value there is $S(50)=8775$.
For $m\ge51$, the quadratic is minimized near $m=401/6\approx66.83$; checking integers gives $S(66)=8351$, $S(67)=8350$, $S(68)=8352$.

Thus the minimum is $8350$, attained for example by $f(i)=67$ for $1\le i\le34$, $f(i)=i+33$ for $35\le i\le66$, and $f(i)=100$ for $67\le i\le100$.

Let $S=\operatorname{Im}(f)$. From $f(f(i))=100$ we get $f(s)=100$ for every $s\in S$ and $100\in S$. The condition $|f(i)-f(i+1)|\le1$ forces $S$ to be an interval, so $S=\{m,m+1,\dots,100\}$ for some $m$. Consequently $f(k)=100$ for all $k\ge m$.

The values $f(1),\dots,f(m-1)$ lie in $[m,100]$, form a walk with steps $\le1$, must end at $f(m-1)\in\{99,100\}$ (adjacent to $f(m)=100$), and must cover every integer in $[m,99]$ (since indices $\ge m$ only take the value $100$). Hence $m-1\ge 100-m$, i.e. $m\ge51$.

To minimise $\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}f(i)$ we stay at $m$ as long as possible and then climb by $1$ to $99$. This uses $q=(m-1)-(100-m)=2m-101$ extra copies of $m$, giving
$$\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}f(i)=(2m-100)m+\sum_{j=m+1}^{99}j,\qquad
\sum_{i=m}^{100}f(i)=(101-m)\cdot100.$$
The total is $T(m)=\frac{3m^2-401m}{2}+15050$, a convex quadratic minimised at $m=401/6\approx66.83$, so $m=67$. This yields $T(67)=8350$.

Explicitly: $f(1)=\dots=f(34)=67$, $f(35)=68,\dots,f(66)=99$, $f(67)=\dots=f(100)=100$ satisfies both conditions and attains the bound.

From $f(f(i))=100$, the image $S$ satisfies $f(s)=100$ for all $s\in S$ and $100\in S$.
The Lipschitz condition $|f(i)-f(i+1)|\le1$ forces $S$ to be an interval $[L,100]$, where $L=\min f(i)$.
Thus $f(s)=100$ for every $s\in[L,100]$; in particular $f(L)=f(L+1)=\dots=f(100)=100$.

For $i<L$ we have $f(i)\in[L,100]$ and $f(i)\ge f(i+1)-1$, so the pointwise minimum is
$$f(i)=\max\bigl(L,\,100-(L-i)\bigr).$$

Computing the total sum:
- for $L\le50$: $\displaystyle S(L)=\frac{20000+L-L^2}2$,
- for $L\ge50$: $\displaystyle S(L)=\frac{3L^2-401L+30100}2$.

The second quadratic is minimized at $L=401/6\approx66.83$, so the best integer is $L=67$, giving
$$S(67)=\frac{3\cdot67^2-401\cdot67+30100}2=8350.$$

An attaining function is $f(i)=67$ for $1\le i\le34$, $f(i)=i+33$ for $35\le i\le66$, and $f(i)=100$ for $67\le i\le100$. Its sum is $34\cdot67+\sum_{k=68}^{99}k+34\cdot100=8350$, and it satisfies both conditions. Hence the minimum possible value is $8350$.

Let $a_i=f(i)$. From $f(f(i))=100$ the image $V=\{a_i\}$ satisfies $v\in V\Rightarrow a_v=100$, and $100\in V$ so $a_{100}=100$. Because $|a_i-a_{i+1}|\le1$, any $v\in V$ forces every integer between $v$ and $100$ to also lie in $V$; hence $V=[m,100]$ for $m=\min V$. Consequently $a_k=100$ for all $k\in[m,100]$, while $a_1,\dots,a_{m-1}\in[m,100]$ and must realise every value $m,m+1,\dots,99$. Thus $m-1\ge100-m$, i.e. $m\ge51$.

For $i<m$, Lipschitz distance to $a_m=100$ gives $a_i\ge100-(m-i)$, and $a_i\ge m$, so
$$a_i\ge L_i:=\max\{m,\;i+100-m\}.$$
The choice $a_i=L_i$ ($i<m$), $a_i=100$ ($i\ge m$) satisfies all constraints whenever $m\ge51$, and it is pointwise minimal. Hence the minimal sum for a given $m$ is
$$S(m)=\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}\max(m,i+100-m)+(101-m)\cdot100.$$
Evaluating $S(m)$ for $m=51,\dots,100$ (or minimising the quadratic $S(m)=\tfrac32m^2-\tfrac{401}2m+\text{const}$) gives the minimum at $m=67$:
$$S(67)=34\cdot67+\sum_{k=68}^{99}k+34\cdot100=4950+3400=8350.$$
